summary: This Standards Track document describes an RTP payload format for V3C atlas sub-bitstreams from ISO/IEC 23090-5 volumetric video coding. It allows packetization of one or more V3C units. The video sub-bitstreams use payload formats defined for their codecs.

eli5.summary: 3D video is cut into little pieces to be sent over the internet, with a way to put them back together.

questions: rtp payload format for volumetric video
how are v3c atlas nal units packetized
subtitle: How to carry the atlas data of 3D volumetric video in RTP packets, and how to tie it to its 2D video streams.

tldr.problem: Volumetric (3D) video coded with V3C is split into video components and atlas data, and the atlas data had no RTP payload format for real-time streaming.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three payload structures for V3C atlas NAL units (single, aggregation and fragmentation), media type parameters, and SDP rules that group the atlas stream with its video streams.
tldr.outcome: Together with the existing RTP payload formats for the video codecs, it gives a complete way to stream V3C-coded content. It is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 10034 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2026. The unit metadata lists nothing that obsoletes or updates it, so it is the current definition of the V3C atlas RTP payload format.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Volumetric video captures an object or scene in three dimensions, so it can be played back independent of the original capture position or orientation. Uncompressed, it is a large amount of data. The visual volumetric video-based coding (V3C) specification, ISO/IEC 23090-5, reduces that data by reusing existing 2D video codecs such as AVC/H.264, HEVC/H.265 or VVC/H.266.

A V3C encoder turns volumetric frames into a collection of 2D frames plus associated data called atlas data. The 2D frames are coded with an ordinary video codec. The atlas data is coded with V3C's own mechanisms and is represented as Network Abstraction Layer (NAL) units. Because of that, this RFC says its payload format shares design philosophy, security, congestion control and overall implementation complexity with other NAL-unit-based RTP payload formats such as RFC 6184 and RFC 7798.

This document defines the RTP payload format for V3C atlas sub-bitstreams only. The video sub-bitstreams use the payload formats defined for their codecs.
sections.eli5: A 3D video is saved as ordinary flat videos plus a set of instructions for putting them back together in 3D. This RFC is about sending the instructions over the internet.

sections.title: How V3C Content Is Built
sections.content:
A V3C bitstream is a series of V3C units. Each has a V3C unit header and a payload. The payload holds a V3C parameter set, atlas data, or one of the V3C video components: occupancy, geometry, attribute or packed video. Occupancy data says which pixels contribute to the reconstructed 3D representation, geometry gives positions, and attribute data carries properties such as color.

Atlas data is a collection of patches. Each patch points at a region in the video components and carries what a decoder needs to project that region back into 3D space. An atlas frame can be divided into non-overlapping tiles that should be independently decodable.

The V3C unit header is four bytes, and its vuh_unit_type says what the unit holds. Atlas NAL units have a 16-bit NAL unit header with a forbidden zero bit, a 6-bit nal_unit_type, a 6-bit nal_layer_id and a 3-bit nal_temporal_id_plus1.

The RFC recommends signaling the V3C parameter set out of band, because it describes the resources needed to decode the stream. Sending it dynamically in the RTP stream might lead to undefined behavior if the receiver lacks the needed capabilities.
sections.eli5: Think of a flat-pack wardrobe. The flat boards are the video, and the instruction sheet is the atlas data. You need both to build it, and this RFC is about sending the instruction sheet.

sections.title: RTP Header and Payload Header
sections.content:
The RTP header is used as in RFC 3550, with a few specific rules. The marker bit is set for the last packet of the access unit carried in the current RTP stream. The payload type is not assigned here and MUST be set through the profile or dynamically. The RTP timestamp is the sampling timestamp of the content, and a 90 kHz clock rate MUST be used.

A NAL unit with no timing of its own, such as a parameter set or SEI NAL unit, takes the RTP timestamp of the coded atlas of the access unit it belongs to. Receivers MUST use the RTP timestamp for the display process, even when the bitstream carries atlas frame timing SEI messages.

The first two bytes of every RTP payload are the payload header, laid out like a NAL unit header with the fields F, NUT, NLI and TID. If a network element detects bit errors it SHOULD set F to 1, and a receiver discards such a packet and conceals the lost data. The TID value MUST NOT be 0.
sections.eli5: Every envelope has a label on the front. The label says what kind of thing is inside, and a clock stamp tells the receiver when to show it.

sections.title: The Three Payload Structures
sections.content:
A receiver tells the three payload structures apart from the NAL unit type in the payload header.

A single NAL unit packet contains exactly one NAL unit. The payload header MUST be an exact copy of the NAL unit header, optionally followed by a 16-bit DONL field and a 16-bit v3c-tile-id field, then the NAL unit payload.

An aggregation packet (AP) wraps two or more NAL units of the same access unit to cut overhead for small ones. Its NUT MUST be 56. Each aggregation unit carries a 16-bit NALU size and the NAL unit, and optionally DOND/DONL and tile id fields. An AP must fit into an IP packet and SHOULD be smaller than the local MTU.

A fragmentation unit (FU) splits one NAL unit over several RTP packets. Its NUT MUST be 57. It adds an 8-bit FU header with a start bit S, an end bit E and a 6-bit FUT field that equals the fragmented NAL unit type. Fragments MUST be sent in consecutive order with ascending sequence numbers, aggregation packets MUST NOT be fragmented, FUs MUST NOT be nested, and S and E MUST NOT both be 1. If an FU is lost, the receiver SHOULD discard the following FUs of the same NAL unit unless its decoder can handle incomplete NAL units.
sections.eli5: Small notes can share one envelope, which is an aggregation packet. A huge note is cut into pieces sent in separate envelopes, marked first, middle and last, which is fragmentation. Anything else goes alone.

sections.title: Decoding Order and Packetization Rules
sections.content:
Packets may arrive in an order that differs from the order a decoder needs. The optional decoding order number (DON) restores it. The parameter sprop-max-don-diff controls this: when it is greater than 0 for any of the RTP streams, the DONL field MUST be present and NAL units may be sent out of decoding order. When it is 0 for all streams, transmission order MUST equal decoding order and the DON fields MUST NOT be present. The RFC defines a variable AbsDon that handles wrap-around of the 16-bit DON values at 65536.

For packetizing, small NAL units SHOULD go into aggregation packets, and each non-ACL NAL unit SHOULD, when it fits the MTU, be aggregated with its associated ACL NAL unit. Exactly one NAL unit in a packet MUST use a single NAL unit packet.

On the receiving side, NAL units with types 0 to 55 may be passed to the decoder, while NAL-unit-like structures with types 56 to 63 MUST NOT be. The RFC calls its de-packetization rules an example, since the process is implementation dependent.
sections.eli5: If the numbered pages of a story arrive shuffled, the page numbers let you put them back in order before you read.

sections.title: Media Type Parameters
sections.content:
The payload format is registered as media type application/v3c. Its one required parameter is sprop-v3c-parameter-set, a base64-encoded v3c_parameter_set(). Optional parameters describe the stream. They include sprop-v3c-unit-header (the 4 bytes of V3C unit header, base64-encoded), separate fields for unit type, parameter set id, atlas id, attribute index and so on, tile id lists, out-of-band atlas data, common atlas data and SEI NAL units, profile-tier-level values (v3c-ptl-*), and sprop-max-don-diff, which may be 0 to 32767.

When sprop-v3c-unit-header is present, the separate parameters it duplicates MUST NOT be present, so that conflicting information cannot be signaled. A receiver MUST ignore any parameter that is not specified.
sections.eli5: These are the settings printed on the shipping label, such as what the package holds and which rules the sender followed.

sections.title: Signaling with SDP
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new SDP attribute, a=v3cfmtp, to carry V3C format parameters at session or media level. It works like a=fmtp but without the format token. For atlas components the media name MUST be application, the encoding name MUST be v3c and the clock rate MUST be 90000. V3C video components use media name video with any video subtype.

A new grouping type, a=group:V3C, lists the media lines (by their mid values) that make up one V3C representation, using the framework of RFC 5888. Examples cover several video components plus an atlas component, and content with two atlases.

In offer/answer (RFC 3264), the offerer lists all V3C components and the answerer may accept them or select a subset by setting the port to zero for unwanted media lines. The profile-tier-level parameters MUST be used symmetrically, except that in unicast the level may be lowered. For multicast the level is not changeable. The RFC also shows an offer that bundles components per RFC 9143.
sections.eli5: Before the show starts, the sender and receiver swap a list of what streams exist and which go together. The receiver says which ones it wants.

sections.title: Congestion Control and Security
sections.content:
Congestion control follows RFC 3550 and the applicable RTP profile, and this part covers unicast only. Users of this format MUST monitor packet loss. Loss is acceptable if a TCP flow on the same path would get no more throughput than the RTP flow. Options include adapting quality of the video components, dropping less important sub-streams, or leaving the session, for example with a circuit breaker per RFC 8083.

For security, the RFC points to the RTP specification and to the applicable profile, and does not mandate a mechanism. It names (D)TLS and IPsec as options. A V3C session can use several RTP streams, so source authentication SHOULD be applied to all of them. The format is not expected to cause denial-of-service through pathological data, it contains no active content, and components SHALL NOT construct payloads with executable content.
sections.eli5: If the road gets jammed, the sender should send less so traffic keeps moving. Everyone should also check that the packages really come from who they say.

fields.name: F
fields.desc: Forbidden zero bit; 1 means possible errors.

fields.name: NUT
fields.desc: NAL unit type; 56 for AP, 57 for FU.

fields.name: TID
fields.desc: Temporal id plus 1; MUST NOT be 0.

fields.name: S
fields.desc: Start of a fragmented NAL unit.

fields.name: E
fields.desc: End of a fragmented NAL unit.

fields.name: FUT
fields.desc: Equals the type of the fragmented NAL unit.
